Russian Missile Strike Kills 10 in Kharkiv Region as Drone Barrage Hits Kyiv — A Russian missile strike on Pechenyhy in the Kharkiv region killed 10 people and injured 8, local authorities said. Russia also launched 147 drones overnight, hitting civilian infrastructure near Kyiv and killing 2 people in Zaporizhzhia.

637 Drones Target Moscow Region as Wildberries Warehouses Suffer Billions in Losses — Russian officials said 637 Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow and the surrounding region overnight on Aug. 17-18, with several people injured and infrastructure damaged. A Wildberries warehouse caught fire, adding to mounting losses from repeated strikes on the e-commerce giant’s logistics network.

Britain Hits Back at Russian Threats Over Ukraine’s Use of British Drones — Britain rejected Russian threats over Ukraine’s reported use of British-made drones, saying its support for Kyiv will continue.

What Is Happening to Russia’s Rear? How Ukraine Shattered the Kremlin’s Sanctuary — Ukraine’s long-range drone campaign is eroding Russia’s rear-area security, while even Kremlin-controlled television acknowledges the growing reach of Ukrainian strikes.

Melania Trump Helps Reunite Another Child With Family Amid Russia’s War — US First Lady Melania Trump facilitated another family reunification as efforts continue to return children separated by Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Russia Threatens UK Over British-Made Drones Allegedly Used in Ukrainian Deep Strikes — Russia accused Britain of escalating its involvement in the war after reports that UK-made drones were used in Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian territory.

Russia Summons Japanese Ambassador After Tokyo Protests Putin’s Kuril Islands Visit — Russia summoned Japan’s ambassador after Tokyo protested President Vladimir Putin’s visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, escalating an already bitter territorial row.

North Korea, Russia Reaffirm Ties on Korean Liberation Day Anniversary — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed deepening of ties on Sunday, Aug. 16, as Moscow-Pyongyang military cooperation continues to grow. The exchange came alongside US President Donald Trump’s sudden halt of US-South Korea joint drills and as Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands for the first time on Aug. 13.

Russia Deliberately Sends Drones Into Moldovan Airspace, Moldovan President Says — Moldovan President Maia Sandu said some drones entering the country’s airspace are not accidental strays, but rather deliberately sent there by Russia. She added that expelling Russia’s ambassador would not stop the violations.

Zelensky Formally Replaces Logistics Forces Commander Karpenko, Appoints Pohribny — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree on Monday, Aug. 17, formally ousting Volodymyr Karpenko as commander of the Logistics Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) and appointing Yuriy Pohribny in his position.

Russia’s Supreme Court Upholds Yabloko Ban, Sentences Deputy Chairman to 11 Years in Prison — Russia’s Supreme Court on Monday, Aug. 17, upheld a ruling barring Yabloko, the country’s only registered liberal party, from September’s parliamentary elections. Separately, Yabloko’s deputy chairman, Lev Shlosberg
was sentenced to 11 years in prison. The decision follows an Aug. 10 lawsuit that accused the party of receiving foreign funding and promoting “extremism.”

Russia Faces New Fuel Shortage, Gasoline Sales Fall 20% — Fuel shortages have returned across parts of Russia after drone attacks damaged oil refineries and seasonal demand increased. Authorities in at least 10 regions have tightened fuel sales restrictions, while gasoline sales fell 20%.

Russia Recruits Ukrainian Teenagers to Build Drones that Attack Ukraine — Russia’s Alabuga Polytechnic University is recruiting teens, including 15- to 17-year-old minors from occupied Ukraine, into paid work-study programs feeding Russia’s Shahed drone industry. Employing underage workers from occupied territory in war work is a war crime, but Russia says it’s helping children.

Baker Tilly to Audit Ukraine’s Defense Procurement Agency After Stormy Year of Disputes — The Defense Procurement Agency’s Supervisory Board has selected Baker Tilly Ukraine to conduct an independent financial audit for 2025. The audit is intended to assess financial reporting, resource use, and financial discipline as the agency works to strengthen transparency and governance.

Russia to Free Up Manpower by Replacing Border Troops With North Korean Soldiers, Ukraine Says — A spokesman for the Ukrainian Volunteer Army said on Monday that Russia might replace up to 20,000 border troops with North Korean soldiers to reinforce the active sectors on the front line. The statement came after Zelensky warned that North Korea might send up to 50,000 soldiers to Russia, while Western intelligence suggests that Russia is delaying its mobilization plans despite high battlefield lo

Russia’s Jet Drones Are Changing the Air War, Ukraine Racing to Respond — Russia is increasingly using jet-powered and missile drones that can reach Ukraine faster and complicate air defense. Experts say the weapons are unlikely to replace Shaheds or cruise missiles entirely, while Ukraine is developing faster interceptor and strike drones of its own.

Binance Gave Russia Data on User Who Donated to Ukraine — Binance gave Russian investigators transaction and personal data on a Russian IT specialist who donated cryptocurrency to Ukrainian military-related causes, Reuters found. The information was later used as evidence in a “terrorism” financing case.

Ukraine War Damage Rises to $197.5B, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute estimates direct damage to Ukraine at $197.5 billion as of February 2026, up 16% from November 2024. Housing remains the hardest-hit sector at $65.9 billion, followed by transport at $42 billion. Energy-sector damage rose 25% to $18.3 billion.

August 18 – An Important Day for Ukrainian Parliamentarism and the Political System — Parliament’s August 18 vote on the appointment of Ukraine’s new defense minister is seen as a crucial test for the country’s political system, amid uncertainty over President Zelensky’s nominee and ongoing public distrust following Mykhailo Fedorov’s dismissal.

Ukraine Says Russian Explosives Plant Hit, Two Workshops Destroyed — Ukraine’s General Staff said a nighttime strike on Russia’s Kamensky Combine destroyed two workshops and damaged four others at a plant producing explosives, gunpowder, and solid rocket fuel.

UK Prime Minister Exchanged Messages With Fake White House Chief of Staff — UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged several messages with someone posing as Trump’s chief of staff Susie Wiles before becoming suspicious. The British embassy raised the incident with the White House and implied “national security” issues could have been discussed, while 10 Downing Street avows “no significance” to communiques.

Russia Places Son of RFK Jr. on Wanted List for Fighting in Ukraine — Conor Kennedy joined Ukraine’s International Legion in 2022, at the onset of Russia’s full-scale invasion, and is believed to have departed in October the same year after a brief stint. A Moscow court has accused him of mercenarism and placed him on its wanted list in August, with a seven- to 10-year sentence.

Russia Turns to 1-3-Man Infiltration Groups as Offensive Stalls Across Multiple Fronts — Russian forces continued offensive operations across several sectors on Aug. 15-16 but made no confirmed advances, ISW says. Moscow’s troops increasingly relied on small infiltration groups, glide-bomb strikes and claims of territorial gains that Ukrainian and Russian sources disputed.

Patriot Missiles Are Running Short Worldwide, Ukraine Faces Winter Threat — Ukraine is struggling to secure enough Patriot interceptors ahead of winter as shortages affect the US and Europe, while a proposed Ukrainian production deal faces major technical and political hurdles.

While Waiting for Patriots, Explosions Are Not Successful Intercepts, They’re Russian Missiles Hitting Civilian Targets — Explosions at night are not air defenses intercepting Russian terror weapons, it’s those ballistic missiles hitting civilian warehouses of supermarkets, e-tailers, and delivery services. Ukrainian’s respond by dispersing goods to stores, or smaller facilities, and signs in shops saying: “This item is unavailable because it was destroyed by Russians.” Zelensky, meanwhile, puts

Top EU Diplomat Seeks Increase in Sanctioned Russian Entities — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas is pushing for the bloc’s most sweeping sanctions listings against Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The proposed measures could increase the number of sanctioned Russian individuals and entities by one-third.

Russia Builds Drone Bases Near NATO, Putting Poland Within Reach — Russia has built at least 10 new drone bases near its borders with Ukraine and Belarus, with dozens of launch rails capable of supporting its latest long-range attack drones. The expansion could eventually put NATO territory, including Warsaw, within range of Moscow’s growing drone arsenal.

‘Cultural Center’ or Spy Hub? Berlin Weighs Russian House Closure — Germany is considering closing Berlin’s Russian House amid allegations that the Kremlin-backed cultural center is being used for propaganda and espionage. The move reflects growing scrutiny of Russian institutions in Germany as Berlin steps up efforts to counter Moscow’s expanding hybrid threat.

Trump Says US Scaling Back Military Drills With Seoul Hours Before Start — US President Donald Trump has ordered the Pentagon to scale back annual US-South Korean military drills, citing his relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The move comes as Pyongyang deepens military ties with Moscow and sends troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Hayden Panettiere, ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville’ Star and Wladimir Klitschko’s Former Fiancée, Dies at 36 — Hollywood actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for Heroes and Nashville, has died at 36, according to US media. She was the former fiancée of Ukrainian boxing legend Wladimir Klitschko, with whom she shared a daughter. Her family has not disclosed the cause of death.

Thousands March in Kyiv, Protestors Demand Zelensky Listens — Thousands rallied peacefully in central Kyiv on Sunday, urging President Volodymyr Zelensky to explain the dismissal of former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and to restore him to the post. Protestors denounced corruption, criticized Zelensky’s inner circle, and demanded accountability ahead of parliament’s Aug. 18 vote on a new defense minister.Author:: Sergii Kostezh

US Military YouTuber Paid His Own Way to Cover Ukraine's Front Line — Justin Taylor, a former US Army infantry officer turned YouTuber, self-funded a two-week reporting trip to Ukraine's front line. He spent nearly a week near active fighting and witnessed drone attacks nightly. He was struck by Ukraine's improvised tech – coordinating via WhatsApp and Zoom instead of encrypted military systems – yet matching costlier Western capabilities. Taylor argues continued US/NATO support remains vital, c

Ukraine’s Onofriichuk Wins Gold at Gymnastics World Championships — Ukrainian gymnast Taisiia Onofriichuk secured the gold medal in the hoop exercise at the Rhythmic Gymnastics World Championships in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, scoring 30.700 points. Italy’s Sofia Raffaeli took silver, and Germany’s Darja Varfolomeev won bronze. The victory marks Onofriichuk’s first career world title and Ukraine’s first World Championship gold in rhythmic gymnastics since 2013.

‘This Evil Must Be Defeated’: Systematic Russian Torture — Oleh Kotov was abducted by Russian invasion forces in April 2022. He endured the full range of Russian torture practices. In June, he was released in a prisoner exchange – the last days of his life he spent in freedom.

Drone Strike Hits Nova Poshta Depot Near Odesa, Injuring 4 — Russian forces struck a Nova Poshta logistics facility located inside an Epicentr shopping center on the outskirts of Odesa on Aug. 16. Odesa Regional Military Administration Head Oleh Kiper reported that a 42-year-old woman and a 32-year-old man were hospitalized with shrapnel wounds following the attack by a “jet-powered drone.” The attack follows a broader wave of strikes on civilian infrastructure across Ukraine, including a deadly

Russia Limits Fuel Sales After Ukrainian Drone Strikes on Refineries — Following Ukrainian drone strikes on oil refineries, Russian regions are imposing fuel sales limits. In the Orenburg region, purchases are capped at 30 liters per car after an attack on the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery. The Novosibirsk region has capped fuel retail markups at 15%. In occupied Crimea, where fuel prices spiked up to 270 rubles ($3) per liter during a brief period of open sales, authorities have implemented stric

Russia’s Powerplay in Sudan Continues — Russia has long tried to make inroads into Africa. In Sudan, the Wagner-assisted rebellion has caused havoc. Even after the rebranding of Wagner, Russia is still undermining the government in Sudan as it tries to secure a naval base in the Red Sea.

Russian Attacks Destroy ArcelorMittal in Kryvyi Rih and Kyiv Book Market — Russian missile and drone strikes on Aug. 16 targeted civilian and industrial infrastructure across Ukraine. In Kryvyi Rih, a strike on the ArcelorMittal mining and metallurgical plant killed two workers, injured 13, and partially halted production. In Kyiv, an attack caused a large-scale fire that destroyed sections of the historic Petrivka book market. The attacks come as President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russi

Ukraine Disables 7 of 10 Largest Wildberries Warehouses — The Ukrainian Defense Ministry stated on Aug. 16 that it has successfully disabled seven of the ten largest logistics centers belonging to the Russian e-commerce platform Wildberries. The announcement followed drone strikes in the Moscow region that caused large fires at the company’s 250,000-square-meter (2,691,000 square-feet) Koledino complex and the Severnoye Domodedovo facility, forcing them to halt operations. The strikes are part o

Lithuania Does Not Rule Out ‘False Flag’ in Latvia Drone Incident — Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said it cannot be ruled out that the drone shot down over Latvia on Aug. 14 was part of a “false flag” operation, though he emphasized that evidence is pending the drone’s recovery. Sinkevičius explained that experts expect to trace the drone’s origin and target using its microchips once found. The incident follows warnings from Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas that Russ

The Iran War Toll — The Iran war failed to achieve regime change or dismantle its nuclear program, instead rallying Iranians behind a more radical leadership. It drained scarce US air-defense missiles needed in Ukraine and Taiwan, pushed oil prices higher while fueling Russia's war chest, and let Iran leverage control of the Strait of Hormuz. Perhaps most damaging: allies like Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are now hedging away from Washington, accelerating a broader erosion of US alliances

Spanish F-18 Downs Unidentified Drone in Romanian Airspace — A Spanish F-18 fighter jet on combat patrol shot down an unidentified drone over Romania early Sunday morning, Aug. 16, after the object breached national airspace from Moldova. The Romanian Defense Ministry reported the drone was intercepted over an unpopulated area in Galați County. Acting Defense Minister Radu Miruță praised the allied response. The interception follows a series of recent airspace violations, including the discovery

Over 1,550 Drones, 62 Missiles Target Ukraine in One Week — Russian forces launched over 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 aerial bombs, and 62 missiles—primarily ballistic – at Ukraine over the past week, President Volodymyr Zelensky reported on Sunday, Aug. 16. Zelensky detailed recent casualty figures, noting two dead and 14 injured in Kryvyi Rih, six injured in Kyiv and the surrounding region, and one dead in Sumy. Thirteen regions were targeted in total. Zelensky urged European partners to

Ukraine Strikes Russian Rocket Fuel Plant in Rostov Region — The Armed Forces of Ukraine reported striking the Kombinat Kamensky enterprise in Russia’s Rostov region on early Sunday morning, Aug. 16. The facility produces solid rocket fuel for multiple launch rocket systems and aviation munitions. A fire was recorded at the site. The General Staff also confirmed damage to the Zapsibneftekhim petrochemical complex in the Tyumen region following an Aug. 10 strike, and to multiple refining units at

On-the-Lam Polish Politician Surfaces in Renegade, Pro-Moscow Moldova Territory — Polish ex-Deputy Justice Minister Marcin Romanowski, wanted for $27M embezzlement (up to 25 years), lives in Transnistria’s Tiraspol beyond Interpol reach. He wants safe conduct to face trial but prosecutors see him as a flight risk after over 18 months on the run.

Russian Drone Strike on Car in Sumy Kills Man, Injures Woman — A Russian drone struck a civilian car in the northeastern city of Sumy late Saturday, Aug. 15, killing a 59-year-old man and injuring his wife. Sumy Regional Military Administration Head Oleh Hryhorov reported the vehicle caught fire following the strike.

Russia Unveils Jet-Powered BM-35 Drone With 217 Mph Speed — Russian propagandists released footage of an upgraded, jet-powered BM-35 attack drone. According to Ukrainian expert Serhii Beskrestnov, the Russians claim the drone can reach speeds exceeding 350 km/h (217 mph) and strike targets up to 200 kilometers (124 miles) away. The drone reportedly carries a 10-kilogram warhead and can be operated in first person view (FPV) mode, allegedly unaffected by electronic warfare.

Ukraine Tests Last Shadow T200 Interceptor Drone, Exceeding Expected Range — Ukrainian defense developer Ukrainska Bavovna has successfully tested the new “Last Shadow T200” interceptor drone, achieving a range of 122 kilometers (76 miles) during recent combat trials – well beyond the originally anticipated 70 kilometers (43 miles). The T200 is designed to defend against Russian Shahed, Geran, Gerbera, and Molniya drones, featuring a top speed of 300 km/h and an operational ceiling of 5 kilomete

Ukrainian Navy Strikes Russian Bastion Missile System in Crimea — The Ukrainian Navy reported striking the launch positions and deployment site of a Russian Bastion coastal missile system in occupied Crimea early morning Sunday, Aug. 16. The military stated the strike resulted in significant, though unspecified, losses to Russian weapons and personnel. The Bastion system is a scarce asset used by Russia to launch supersonic Onyx and hypersonic Zircon missiles at Ukrainian territory.

Poland Proposes European Legion With Ukrainian Veterans — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski advocated for the creation of a permanent “European Legion” during an interview with Ekathimerini. He suggested the force could recruit combat-experienced Ukrainian veterans post-war to bolster European defense capabilities. Sikorski emphasized that Europe must take greater responsibility for its security rather than relying solely on the US, while maintaining that the proposed force would complem

Gulf Allies Question US Ties Over Iran Conflict — US allies in the Persian Gulf, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, are increasingly frustrated with US President Donald Trump’s diplomatic approach to the war with Iran. Regional officials cite unpredictable policy shifts and have begun questioning the necessity of hosting US military bases. The discontent follows a recent mutual defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, indicating a push to diversify security partnerships.

Russian Strikes Devastate Metinvest’s Zaporizhstal Factory, Epicentr Mall in Zaporizhzhia — Successive Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia have severely damaged Ukraine’s industrial and retail sectors. Overnight Aug. 10-11, a ballistic missile strike killed seven workers and forced a complete shutdown of Metinvest’s Zaporizhstal steel plant. Early on Aug. 12, a Russian strike destroyed an Epicentr shopping centre in a residential area, causing a massive fire.

‘No Room for Mistakes’: What Next for Protestors Demanding Fedorov’s Reinstatement? — The protests against Mykhailo Fedorov’s dismissal as minister of defense are increasingly expanding in focus, reflecting broader public concerns about corruption, non-transparent decision-making, and the government’s lack of accountability. Although a major rally is planned for Aug. 16, it remains unclear whether the protests will continue if Fedorov is not reinstated, especially as Fedorov himself has neither

Ukraine’s  Mahuchikh Wins Third Consecutive European High Jump Gold — Ukrainian athlete Yaroslava Mahuchikh won gold in the women’s high jump at the 2026 European Athletics Championships in Birmingham, England, clearing 1.97 meters on her first attempt. This marks her third consecutive European title following victories in 2022 and 2024. Poland’s Maria Zhodzik took silver and Montenegro’s Marija Vukovic won bronze, both clearing 1.95 meters. Fellow Ukrainian Iryna Herashchenko finished fifth wit

Drone Attacks Spark Large Fires at Wildberries Hubs Near Moscow — A large-scale drone attack on the Moscow region early Sunday morning resulted in massive fires at two major logistics centers: the 200,000-square-meter (2,150,000 square-feet) Wildberries facility in Koledino and the Severnoye Domodedovo complex. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin claimed air defenses downed 105 drones, while operations at Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports were suspended. Separately, explosions were reported l

Russian Strikes on Kryvyi Rih and Kyiv Leave 2 Dead, 16 Injured — Russian forces launched combined ballistic missile and drone attacks on Kryvyi Rih and Kyiv early Sunday morning, Aug. 16. In Kryvyi Rih, strikes on industrial facilities left two people dead and 13 injured, while a separate attack in the Nikopol district injured another individual. In Kyiv, missile strikes caused fires and damage in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts, injuring three people.
